scope: Assigned frozen titles and complete ItemBodies, local rendered HTML, and every assigned screenshot tile; no live routes.

review_method.normative_instructions: CLAUDE.md read fully; README.md read fully; tools/autopilot/AUDIT.md consulted for audit boundaries and local-only workflow.
review_method.rendering: Every assigned local PNG tile was opened individually with tools.view_image at original resolution; no collage or downscaling.
review_method.source_snapshot_html: Every assigned title and complete ItemBody was reviewed from the frozen snapshot and compared with the matching local HTML and tile sequence; source, snapshot, HTML, receipt and image hashes were checked against their inventories.
review_method.boundary: No live route or network access; no item, application, or publication-status edits; no builds, tests, gates, commits or pushes. Only lane-03.md and lane-03.json were written.

optional_typography.observation: Wikilinks styled as block links can place adjacent commas, periods, and closing punctuation on separate lines. This is visible in the supplied HTML and tiles and is not treated as a defect. No raw TeX/TikZ, malformed mathematical notation, clipped item content, or diagram mismatch was found.

diagram_candidates.rationale: The algorithm specifies a long chronological word on the ordered wires (a,b,t), with a clean work bit and an identical repeated block. A three-wire diagram would make the target, ancilla use, and complete wire scope easier to scan than the numbered gate list.
diagram_candidates.draw_or_check: Draw exactly three horizontal wires a, b, t from left to right, with t initialized and returned to |0>. Render steps 1–5 as the stated chronological gate sequence, then repeat the same 15-gate block from steps 1–4; preserve every T/T† label and CNOT control-target direction. The target controlled-T action is on a,b and the diagram must not imply an extra wire. Confirm against the exact order in lines 37–43 and the return/proposition claim in lines 50–53; diagram is explanatory, not proof.
diagram_candidates.status: Optional; the complete chronological gate list already specifies the circuit.

diagram_candidates.kind: relative square-lattice and dual-lattice path diagram
diagram_candidates.rationale: The statement and proof distinguish a primal rough-to-rough Z path of minimum length d from a top-to-bottom dual X path of minimum length d+1, and use disjoint cuts and deleted rough boundary edges. One small labelled patch diagram would make the boundary convention and primal/dual path relationship substantially easier to follow.
diagram_candidates.draw_or_check: For a small representative d (e.g. d=3), draw the (d+1)×(d+1) primal vertex grid, mark left/right rough boundaries and show the 2d² retained physical edges after deleting the 2d rough vertical boundary edges. Overlay a straight horizontal Z logical row crossing each of the d vertical cuts. In a second aligned layer or contrasting color, show the dual graph with top/bottom exterior vertices and a straight top-to-bottom X path crossing d+1 horizontal cuts; indicate one odd crossing with the Z row. Keep face checks and boundary checks in the convention of line 54–55. Do not use the diagram as a proof of the rank or path-count claims.
diagram_candidates.status: Optional; the proof is self-contained, and its incidence/path arguments are exact.

limitations: Local frozen previews only. This is a rendering and diagram-opportunity review, not a full mathematical audit; no live production route was inspected.
